I beleive that depends on what kind of plant it is. From my basic knowledge of plants, there are two kinds:

  • Auto-flowering, meaning they grow until a certain size then flower

  • Photo-period flowering, meaning they will grow or flower based on the ratio of light/dark hours they get. They can tell what season it is based off of light, not temperature. This is how a lot of deciduous trees decide when to shed leaves/grow buds. If it were based on temperature they would jump the gun after the first cold day in the autumn or the first warm day early in the spring.
